response: Assessing joint line positions by means of the contralateral knee can be a useful approach for planning knee revision surgery. This method involves comparing the joint line position of the affected knee to that of the unaffected, contralateral knee. By doing so, surgeons can better determine the optimal joint line position for the revision surgery, which is crucial for restoring normal knee function and preventing complications such as instability, limited range of motion, and pain. This approach can be particularly helpful in cases where the original joint line position is unclear or has been altered due to previous surgeries or trauma.
